tagline: Down the North Loup from the Sand Hills to Danish country.
intro: From Dunning, NE 91 heads northeast through the Sand Hills past Brewster, then turns east into farmland at Taylor and comes over to Burwell. There the byway takes up NE 11, which keeps beside the North Loup River down through Ord to Elba, then runs south through Dannebrog and Cairo to Wood River. Red barns and silos stand along the farm miles.
The Loups take their name from the French for wolf, after the Skidi band of the Pawnee, the Wolf People, who lived along the river.

moments.title: Fort Hartsuff
moments.text: Southeast of Burwell, a cavalry post active only from 1874 to 1881 still has its original headquarters, barracks, officers' quarters and hospital.

moments.title: Ord
moments.text: Ord's own Evelyn Sharp turned 18 in the 1930s and became the youngest woman commercial pilot in the country.

moments.title: Dannebrog
moments.text: Settled in 1871 by a colony of Danes from Milwaukee, the village took its name from the Danish flag, and the Danish Brotherhood's Columbia Hall is among its historic buildings.
